liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Not Fade Away** (2 reviews): The Not Fade Away into Goin' Down the Road into Not Fade Away sequence is singled out as a standout; The reviewer calls the Not Fade Away, Goin' Down the Road, Not Fade Away sequence the best ever [10][18]
- **Sugaree** (1 review): Jerry's Sugaree is singled out as shining, along with Cumberland Blues and Loser [14]
- **Comes A Time** (1 review): Described as beautiful, with some interesting alternate lyrics [10]
- **Dark Star** (1 review): The Dark Star, Drums, Other One, Me and My Uncle, Other One sequence is praised, including the jams between songs [16]
- **The Other One** (1 review): The first Other One is called thunderous [10]

## Setlist highlights

- **Hide Away**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 4 archived performances [22]
- **station id - tuning**: rare: 3 archived performances [22]
- **station id - tuning**: rare: 3 archived performances [22]
- **station id - tuning**: rare: 3 archived performances [22]

## The recordings

- **gd1971-11-07.127503.fm.boswell.smith.flac16** (recommended): FM broadcast; 34 songs; 207 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1971-11-07.167790.FM.Menke-Miller.flac1648**: FM broadcast; 31 songs; 233 min [3]. Said about its sound: Mix issues at the start of Ramble On Rose on all sources; Brokedown Palace has an extra reel generation [3]
- **gd71-11-07.prefm.kaplan.9570.sbeok.shnf**: pre-FM broadcast master; 31 songs; 214 min; rated 4.5/5 by 42 [5]. Said about its sound: Pre-FM reels have dropouts in Brown Eyed Women and mostly distorted piano; a 2nd-generation cassette of the FM broadcast sounds better in some ways; The pre-FM sound quality is weaker than most archive shows, though the ear adjusts after a few songs; The piano feed is distorted, and there are a few other flaws [12][13][14][17][18][21]
- **gd1971-11-07.155687.remastered.boswell.smith.miller.flac24**: FM broadcast; 31 songs; 220 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [7]
- **gd1971-11-07.169935.prefm.gdh.miller.flac1644**: pre-FM broadcast master; 31 songs; 194 min [9]

## Around the show

- The Harding is an old historic theater with comfy chairs and cool lights, giving an intimate, living-room feel [14]
- The band sounds laid back and relaxed, with stage banter [21]
- New Riders of the Purple Sage opened; there were monitor issues throughout the first set [3]
- The reviewer sees it as a nice lead-up to the December shows [17]
- The 11/6/71 show sounds better: the bass is more solid and the piano rattle is less bad [20]
- Reviewer does not rank it as the best of 1971 and says there are better shows that year [21]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1971-11-07.127503.fm.boswell.smith.flac16**: taped by Peter Kafer; transferred by Will Boswell; Matt Smith; source: FM MR @ 3/ 3.4 ips(Peter Kafer?)>R @ 3 & 3/4 ips(Will Boswell) [1]
- **gd1971-11-07.167790.FM.Menke-Miller.flac1648**: taped by Recording and Transfer by Bob Menke; transferred by Mastering by Charlie Miller  June 11, 2024; source: FM (KSFX-FM) > Master Reels (3.75ips 1/4trk) [3]
- **gd71-11-07.prefm.kaplan.9570.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [5]. Also: Soundboard pre-FM reel transferred to DAT, then CD, via Seth Kaplan [5]
- **gd1971-11-07.155687.remastered.boswell.smith.miller.flac24**: taped by Tape supplied by Will Boswell; transferred by Transfer by Matt Smith Mastering by Charlie Miller  February 12, 2022; source: FM > Master Reel (3.75ips) > Reel (3.75ips) [7]. Also: Remastered from Matt Smith's source, with 17 minutes of tunings and banter patched from another source [7]
- **gd1971-11-07.169935.prefm.gdh.miller.flac1644**: transferred by All Mastering by Charlie Miller  December 26, 2024; source: Pre-FM > Master Reels > DAT (44.1k) [9]. Also: Pre-FM source from a Grateful Dead Hour DAT, with Bob Menke's recording used as patch source [9]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by michaelsmusiclog.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead: “Harding Theater 1971” (2016) CD Review](https://michaelsmusiclog.blogspot.com/2017/09/grateful-dead-harding-theater-1971-2016.html) [23]
